nodes.label: 2026-08-11-relevance-weight-demand-and-facet-measurements.md — working notes for the 2026-08-11 session on the artefact_v1_relevance_weight arm: where its facet signal goes and what that day's runs measured. Everything was read or computed from disk on that date, and it describes that moment. Convention: a line marked [MEASURED] is a quantity computed from disk with the conditions it was computed under; a line marked [READING] is that session's interpretation of one — an agent's opinion, not a finding, and never the user's. Quote the measurement, never the reading.

Read this before anything else: six claims made during the session and measured false inside the same session. 1 'The arm writes to the graph' — false; the arm is read-only, build_facet_layer.py holds the write path and the arm reads the layer from the cache file. 2 'The user already ruled the facet centring at 0.5' — false; his 08-07 approvals answered a list of six measured findings about the concept, 0.5 appeared later as a proposed defect fix, and the centring has never been put to him as a question, so the word derived in the PHI_NEUTRAL row of CONSTANTS.md is an agent's provenance claim, not a ruling. 3 'Moving the clustering geometry to prepare fixes the slow questions' — false; it is 1.5% of the walk it sits in. 4 'The tag path filters instead of lifting, and the interpreter's zeros fire the gate' — false for every run on disk; the gate never fires. 5 'The det recall ordering 0.7439 / 0.7345 / 0.7283 / 0.7188 shows the derived layer losing to the baked one' — not supported; every one of those differences is inside measured run-to-run variation. 6 'The +0.086 from flat to centred is the mechanism working' — that is the arm compared against degraded versions of itself; against the engine already in the tree it is 0.334 against 0.734.

Three standing do-not-conclude traps. Do not read an ordering into the det runs: two runs with byte-identical flags three minutes apart differ on 76 of 100 retrieved id sets and 0.005095 mean recall — the same size as every facet effect measured against them. Do not report a within-arm delta as the arm's standing: flat / read / centred are one arm against itself. Do not apply the interpreter's zero-facet statistics to the det leg: they come from v3/output/interp_cache/, which belongs to the artefact_v1 interpreting leg, and no det run uses it.

Where the arm stands [MEASURED]. artefact_v1_relevance_weight is the arm built 08-08 on the derived facet layer; all figures are context_recall_id, gold-100, k=50, retrieval-only — no generator ran, so every text metric reads 0.0000 by construction and is not a result. artefact_v1_det with HERB_STR_FACET=1.0 and baked facets 0.7439; artefact_v1_det with HERB_STR_FACET=0.0 (the default build) 0.7339 / 0.7345 / 0.7345 / 0.7294; artefact_v1_det with HERB_STR_FACET=1.0 and derived facets 0.7283 / 0.7188; artefact_v1 0.6363; artefact_v1_relevance_weight HERB_DEMAND=centred 0.3340, read 0.2590, flat 0.2477; vector 0.1129; lucene 0.0894. Control-to-control variation, which bounds how any of the above may be read: two artefact_v1_det runs with byte-identical retrieval flags three minutes apart differ on 76 of 100 retrieved id sets and 0.005095 mean recall_id, while the baked facet-live delta is +0.009416 and the two derived deltas are −0.006185 and −0.015683.

Paired per-question, centred against read (n=100) [MEASURED]: context_recall_id flat 0.2477, read 0.2590, centred 0.3340, delta +0.0750, 95% CI [+0.0193, +0.1307], W/L/T 37/28/35; context_precision_id 0.1106 / 0.1055 / 0.0896, delta −0.0159, CI [−0.0494, +0.0177], 30/49/21; context_precision_nonllm 0.1671 / 0.1412 / 0.1136, delta −0.0276, CI [−0.0869, +0.0317], 14/25/61; context_recall_nonllm 0.0300 / 0.0282 / 0.0256, delta −0.0026, CI [−0.0091, +0.0040], 8/16/76. Only recall_id's interval excludes zero. centred also changes what _walk orders areas by, so +0.0750 covers the scoring change and the walk-order change together and is not attributable to the scoring alone. Run directories: flat …20260810T200231Z, read …20260811T084924Z, centred …20260811T104337Z, and the original read of …20260808T071137Z (same value, 0.2590).

What the demand read does [MEASURED]. The arm's edge weighting is <demand, phi_centred>, where demand is a five-facet probability vector (softmax, then shrunk toward uniform by a measured reliability). Across the 100 questions of the read run there are 100 distinct vectors — it is not a constant — with movement confined to two facets: entities mean 0.275 sd 0.042 range 0.179; activity 0.157 / 0.032 / 0.137; evidence 0.181 / 0.008 / 0.038; topic 0.192 / 0.006 / 0.031; temporal 0.195 / 0.003 / 0.013, against flat 0.200 — temporal moves 0.013 across the entire question set. Decomposition of the edge score, the 100 recorded demand vectors against the 67,913 × 5 centred facet layer: the flat term 0.2 · Σ(phi_centred), identical for every query, 94.0%; a fixed tilt, mean demand less flat, also identical for every query, 4.3%; the query-specific residual 1.6%. demand sums to 1, so 0.2 of it is always the flat direction, and every entry is positive — the smallest any facet received across 100 questions is 0.096. Effect on edge orderings: as built, query-to-query correlation 0.985, correlation with a flat profile 0.971 (min 0.899), top-500 edge overlap between queries 90%; centred on the demand's corpus mean, 0.003 / −0.000 / 21%; centred on the flat 0.2 vector, 0.848 / −0.004. The facet layer's five columns are near-independent — largest inter-column correlation +0.21, most under 0.13 — with variance spreading 0.250 / 0.234 / 0.203 / 0.183 / 0.131.

What the five facets are properties of [MEASURED]. Within-group variance share over the built layer (67,913 edges) — varies across a tag's chunks / varies across a chunk's tags: topic 44.7% / 80.5%; evidence 73.5% / 0.0%; temporal 4.1% / 75.9%; entities 0.0% / 87.7%; activity 0.0% / 83.6%. entities and activity are dot products against the tag embedding, so they carry one value per tag regardless of chunk; evidence is the chunk's register profile, so it carries one value per chunk regardless of tag. [READING] Against "tag-facets inform the RELEVANCE of the tag, per facet, relative to its chunk" (06-27, user_turns_all.md:285), four of the five are not per-(tag, chunk) quantities. The user's own position, 08-11, which outranks that reading: the ownership question does not matter much, because the value lives on the edge and is aggregated per edge in routing; what matters is whether the facets work.

The tag layer under all of it [MEASURED]: 19,716 tags, 4,869 chunks, 67,913 edges, 13.9 tags per chunk. A tag reaching 1 chunk is 65.6% of tags and 19.0% of edges; 2 chunks 14.6% / 8.5%; 3–5 chunks 10.6% / 11.3%; 6–20 chunks 6.8% / 19.5%; 21+ chunks 2.4% / 41.7%. Per chunk, 79.6% of its tags are carried by at least one other chunk, and no chunk's tag set is wholly unique to it. The temporal facet's evidence: its estimator measures how concentrated a tag's chunks are in time and needs at least two dated chunks, so 100% of single-chunk tags carry no temporal evidence and 66.3% of the whole vocabulary has none — temporal is the only facet with unevidenced cells (78.2% of edges evidenced against 100% for the other four), its between-tag spread is 0.096 against 0.24–0.31, and its measured ICC is 0.202 against 0.601 for the topic vote. Temporal survives co-occurrence-neighbourhood averaging better than the other facets: 89.3% of its tag-level spread survives against 35–54% for the rest, which rules out dilution-by-averaging as the reason its demand is pinned. The per-facet query-side reliability values the arm used are recorded in meta.reliability per question but in no run manifest, so how much of the pinning is reliability shrinkage versus thin signal underneath was not separated.

Clustering cost [MEASURED]. Region sizes from the read run's own records (500 areas = 100 questions × 5 facets): median 3 tags, mean 526, p90 1,858, max 6,880. Clustering cost scales with the square of region size: 10% of the areas carry 98.4% of it, five questions carry 54.8%, the worst single question carries 12.3%, and 80 of 100 questions together account for under 1%. Everything in _facet_distances — the tag-embedding cosine, the tags' facet marginals, the facet's corpus spread — is a build-time constant; only which tags _region admits depends on the query.

What the geometry precompute bought [MEASURED]. At n ≈ 6,800 the memmap slice is ~350 ms against ~1,000 ms for the matmul; one five-facet walk at n = 6,654 takes 42.5 s sliced against 42.2 s computed — the geometry is ~0.35 s of a ~42 s walk, 1.5%, with the remaining time in the linkage and the best-fit search. A resident float64 table (3.110 GB) overruns the laptop's free memory at the largest region and measured slower than the matmul when paged (932 ms against 586 ms at n = 1,858); float32 is 1.555 GB and not bit-identical (max cell difference 5.96e-08); a packed triangle is 2.1× slower than doing nothing. The memmap is the only exact form that fits. [READING] This session read 1.5% as not worth the 3.110 GB, and read the linkage as where the cost actually is.

Code changed 2026-08-11, uncommitted; artefact_v1_relevance_weight.py has never been committed at all. HERB_DEMAND=centred — a third value beside read (default, untouched) and flat: at prepare it computes the corpus-expected demand by running the same read over the chunk-description probe bank and averaging, and at query time the weighting is demand − expected_demand, unnormalized and unclamped, so entries may be negative. Tag geometry precompute — the full tag-to-tag cosine-distance table built once at prepare as a float64 memmap under v3/output/tag_distance_cache/, keyed by database, tagging run, vocabulary size and a sha256 over the tag names and embedding bytes, with a manifest written last as the completeness marker; _walk slices the region out of it. First build +14.9 s, reuse +104.6 ms, 3.110 GB on disk; the linkage is untouched. Plus tests for both, CONSTANTS.md rows for both (counts to 356), and .gitignore for the cache. Bit-identity of the read and flat paths was proved twice: 200 randomized layers against the expression the centred change replaced (max|diff| 0), and 60 randomized layers across all three regimes against the shipped memmap _walk (518 + 533 + 583 selected rows, max|score diff| 0, meta identical cell for cell).

The det leg, measured while answering a mis-scoped question — these figures are about artefact_v1_det, not the relevance-weight arm, and they stand on their own [MEASURED]. The facet term zeroes nothing in any det run: the det plan sets all five facets to a flat 0.2, no interpreter emits zeros on that leg, no edge carries an exact 0.0 in w_facets, facetTerm spans 0.0600–0.9100 with median 0.4400, and _mod(facetTerm, 1.0) is never 0. Gold-bearing and non-gold chunks are indistinguishable under it: top-50 retrieved pooled over 100 questions, 583 gold-bearing against 4,417 non-gold, exact-zero facet factor 0 and 0, median highest factor 0.6100 against 0.5800; whole graph, every chunk against every question, 996 gold pairs mean 0.6053 against 485,904 non-gold pairs mean 0.5815. Derived-versus-baked is not a facet-only contrast: build_facet_layer.py writes r.w_chunk as well as the facets, w_chunk differs on all 67,913 edges between the baked backup and the derived entry, and w_chunk enters the tag score at STR_WCHUNK = 1.0 regardless of STR_FACET. No run manifest records which facet layer was in the graph, and the two derived runs disagree with each other on 78 of 100 questions. The live herb-eval graph currently holds the baked layer: 67,913 edges compared against the backup, 0 differing on facets, w_facets or w_chunk. The exact tag-reached set is recoverable for only 12 of 100 questions — meta truncates each level's tag list to 6 names, so 159 of 763 walk steps cannot be expanded. Interpreter cache (300 interpretations, 1,006 scored parts): 64.5% of parts carry at least one exact 0.0 facet score — temporal 46.7%, entities 27.2%, activity 17.7%, topic 0.8%, evidence 0.5% — belonging to the interpreting leg, whose STR_FACET also defaults to 0.0, so those zeros have never reached a scored run.

His rulings 2026-08-11, both in the corpus. 11:14 precompute: "ffs, everything that doesnt need to be ran in querytime should be premade!" — recorded under R3 in OPEN_DECISIONS.md; it settles every part of the clustering carrying no query dependence, the whole distance geometry, and it does not settle the linkage, since average-linkage heights depend on which points are present, so a globally-built dendrogram sliced to a region is not the region's own clustering. 12:38 ask first: "tell me what you are doing before running off like this, dude, always ask before" — restating the 07-16 trust revocation; five agents were dispatched that session without an instruction naming them. Open and unverified: DATA_README.md carries no record of this arm at all — not the three runs of that day, not the 08-08 run, not the arm; nothing from that day is committed and the arm has never been committed; the det leg returns different results for identical inputs, unexplained; whether the +0.0750 comes from the scoring change or the walk-order change is not separated, and a centred run with the walk order pinned to the uncentred read would do it; the walk's widening standard is np.median of at most five banked hits, an agent's reading of a hedged question of his (07-20, user_turns_all.md:1745) declared as that agent's own invention, whose prescribed check has never run, with the standard met at entry on 83% of areas; the guide floor is logged in CONSTANTS.md as an arithmetic identity rather than a chosen statistic, an agent's claim, unreviewed; and the 3.110 GB tag distance cache is invalidated by any retag.
